passage: Last Friday night, my phone slipped out of my hand and landed on the stone floor. The screen cracked into a spider web of lines. I picked it up and tried to unlock it, but only half of the screen worked. I felt annoyed because I needed the phone for work. The next morning, I searched for a repair shop online and found one near the metro station. A friendly young man opened the shop door and welcomed me in. He looked at my phone and said the screen needed a new one. He offered two choices: an original screen or a cheaper one. I chose the original because I wanted it to last longer. He asked me to wait for forty minutes. I sat down and drank a cup of tea. When he finished, the phone looked brand new. I paid him and thanked him many times. On the way home, I dropped the phone into my bag very carefully.
